methodological_rigor.justification: Rigorous preclinical study combining high-throughput compound screening (144 cell death-related compounds), multiple independent ovarian cancer cell lines (12 cell lines tested), in vivo xenograft models (BALB/c nude mice, n=8 per group), and patient-derived xenograft/organoid models. Proper controls, dosing schedules specified, technical replicates reported (n=3 for in vitro, n=5-8 for in vivo). Statistical testing appropriate (Student's t-test, two-way ANOVA) with P-values reported. Limitations: single species (mice), limited human sample size for PDX/PDO models.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Preclinical translational research using BRCA-proficient ovarian cancer models to identify therapeutic vulnerabilities to PARPi resistance. Mechanism of action clearly defined: elesclomol-copper binds ATRIP, disrupts ATR-ATRIP interaction, sensitizes to PARPi. Identifies secondary vulnerability in de novo pyrimidine synthesis. Directly relevant to clinical problem of PARPi resistance, but requires in vivo validation and clinical translation before clinical utility established.

reporting_quality.justification: Comprehensive methods section following ARRIVE guidelines for animal studies. All cell lines authenticated with short tandem repeat fingerprinting and mycoplasma testing. Animal protocols approved (ethics approval number specified). Detailed methodology for compound screening, cell viability assays, flow cytometry, RNA-seq (GSE246085 in GEO), metabolomics, and protein interactions. Supplementary data tables referenced (Supplementary Data 1). RNA-seq data deposited in public repository with accession number.

novelty_literature.justification: Novel finding that copper ionophore elesclomol synergizes with PARPi through direct ATRIP binding mechanism. Discovery of de novo pyrimidine synthesis as metabolic vulnerability in PARPi-resistant tumors represents new therapeutic avenue. Combines known components (elesclomol, PARP inhibitors) in novel mechanistic context. Use of 15N-glutamine metabolic tracing and AlphaFold3 predictions for protein interaction modeling demonstrates current-state methodology.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-organized manuscript with clear progression from compound screening to mechanism identification to in vivo validation. Figures effectively communicate key findings (compound heatmap, dose-response curves, xenograft data, mechanistic diagrams). Supplementary figures support main findings comprehensively. Methods section detailed and transparent. Discussion appropriately contextualizes findings within PARPi resistance literature and proposes future translational steps.

key_strengths: Unbiased compound screening of 144 cell death-inducing molecules followed by systematic validation identifies elesclomol-copper synergy with PARPi
Mechanistic clarity: copper directly binds ATRIP protein, disrupts ATR-ATRIP interaction, suppresses ATR-CHK1 repair pathway; validated by Co-IP, PLA, and AlphaFold3 structure prediction
Comprehensive preclinical evidence: efficacy demonstrated in 12 ovarian cancer cell lines, xenografts (ES-2, 3AO), and patient-derived xenograft/organoid models
Identifies secondary therapeutic vulnerability in de novo pyrimidine synthesis pathway, enabling rational combination strategy to overcome PARPi resistance
key_concerns: PDX and PDO models use single patient-derived samples; requires larger patient cohort to assess heterogeneity of metabolic vulnerabilities
Elesclomol (HY-12040) is investigational; clinical translation requires evaluation of toxicity, pharmacokinetics, and drug-drug interactions with PARPi
Metabolomics findings based on targeted analysis; broader metabolic reprogramming in PARPi-resistant tumors may not be fully captured
Study limited to BRCA-proficient cancers; applicability to BRCA-mutant PARPi-resistant disease remains to be determined
chief_reviewer.rationale: Tier 3 paper demonstrates solid preclinical methodology with clear translational relevance and novel mechanistic insights. Strong experimental design with multiple validations, but limited to preclinical models; requires clinical trial initiation to advance treatment paradigm. Appropriate for specialized oncology journal (Cancer Research, Molecular Cancer).
